## Summary

Move only the Android devcontainer's Dockerfile default and `build.args.VARIANT` from `8.0-noble` to the published `mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/dotnet:11.0-resolute` Ubuntu 26.04 image.

This addresses the **Android devcontainer portion of D1** in #136313, not the separate Android Helix VM/queue migration. It does not close the tracking issue or complete all of D1.

Android NDK r27c, command-line SDK `13114758_latest`, API level 35, build tools 35.0.0, the x86_64 system image selection and both archive SHA-256 checksums are unchanged. Packages (including OpenJDK 17), features, developer user/settings, lifecycle hooks, KVM configuration and repository SDK/framework pins are also unchanged. The newer base changes the image's bootstrap SDK; the repository-pinned `.dotnet` PATH precedence is retained. No package/setup workaround is included.

## Validation

Passed static checks:

- `node "$EVIDENCE_DIR/validate-config.cjs"` — passed. The external validation script parses JSONC and compares the complete configuration and Dockerfile with the original HEAD, asserting that only the two approved base selections changed and that exactly those two tracked files differ. `EVIDENCE_DIR` refers to the retained local session evidence directory; this script is not added to the repository.
- `bash -n .devcontainer/scripts/onCreateCommand.sh .devcontainer/scripts/postCreateCommand.sh .devcontainer/android/postStartCommand.sh` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

Before building, the published base's Linux AMD64 manifest was verified as `sha256:5ca289aefffd9a753687cfae8ea5c253a806b4e07dc27b54d088faed1fac69e8` (multi-platform index `sha256:e6f76375a860ad18bbc54f748d78406395af240cae0453030c12adf1bfe8142f`). A disposable base-only container reported Ubuntu 26.04.1 and `amd64`; this was not a completed Android devcontainer smoke test.

Attempted the actual configured feature-enabled image build on an ARM64 Mac using Docker Desktop 4.47.0 **Linux AMD64 emulation**, not native x64 or ARM64 validation:

```sh
npm exec --yes --package @devcontainers/cli@0.89.0 -- devcontainer build \
  --workspace-folder "$PWD" \
  --config "$PWD/.devcontainer/android/devcontainer.json" \
  --platform linux/amd64 \
  --image-name copilot-android-6cfcbeee:validation --no-lockfile
```

**Result: failed, exit 1.** Package setup, including OpenJDK 17, both pinned archive checksum checks, NDK extraction, SDK license acceptance and platform-tools/API 35/build-tools 35.0.0 installation completed. The build then failed committing the x86_64 system-image layer with Docker BuildKit storage/metadata I/O errors:

```text
write /var/lib/docker/buildkit/metadata_v2.db: input/output error
```

No complete feature-enabled image was produced; KVM group setup and feature installation stages were not reached. No devcontainer startup, lifecycle execution, Java/NDK runtime or compiler smoke, shared-library smoke, emulator/AVD execution, KVM validation or full Android product build coverage was established. Destructive/heavy/emulator hooks were inspected but not invoked. No emulation workaround or Docker recovery change was made.

The user explicitly waived further local validation to review and publish this focused patch. The waiver does not turn the failed or unexecuted checks into passes. Ordinary runtime/Android product CI is not evidence that this devcontainer builds, and emulator execution still requires separate validation on a KVM-capable Linux host.
